claimed.claimed_convergence_order_in_N: The paper does NOT claim a convergence in the carrier frequency for the prescribed-amplitude covariance: (7.26) is an identity at every k (order infinity, error zero). Its only N-dependent statements are class bounds (upper bounds): the exactly divergence-free field is curl_* A_m = (t_m + r_m) e^{ikm Phi} with C_m = i n_Phi x t_m/(km |n_Phi|^2) (7.38, p. 86), r_m in W_{alpha+1/2-kappa_s} (Lemma 7.7), i.e. relative eps^{1/2-kappa_s}; under the paper's coupling eps k^2 in [1,4] (p. 74, p. 77, p. 81 'eps k^2 ~ 1 throughout') this is N^{-(1-2 kappa_s)} with N = k, kappa_s = 1e-5 (p. 63). Corollary 7.8 (7.42, p. 87): the covariance defect of the actual field, B(U,R) in M_{alpha+1/2-kappa_s}, i.e. relative N^{-(1-2kappa_s)}, again an upper bound; the radial divergence costs at most a further kappa_s (P2: same exponent). PRE-RUN DERIVATION from the paper's own formulas: for the real cosine pulse the potential is -(n_Phi x t)/(k|n_Phi|^2) sin(k Phi), so the curl remainder multiplies sin(k Phi) while t multiplies cos(k Phi); the cross term B(W_0, R) has <cos sin>_theta = 0 exactly, and the defect is (1/2)<r_r r_tan> with r_r = -D_z C_theta = -eps d_Z C_theta (7.38). Hence the sharp order is faster than the bound: the defect scales like eps^3 (two factors eps^{1/2} from 1/(kB_s), two from D_z, one from the second D_z or slow derivative), i.e. N^{-6} under eps k^2 fixed. INTERPRETATION FIXED NOW, BEFORE ANY NUMBER: because the paper's convergence statements are class memberships (upper bounds), the +-0.3 window of P1/P2 is applied one-sidedly: measured exponent <= claimed + 0.3 passes; a measured exponent more negative than -1 is consistent with the paper and is reported as such; whether the two-sided window is met is reported alongside.
claimed.how_N_is_varied: N = k with the paper's coupling eps k^2 = 4 held fixed (eps := 4/N^2, the ceiling case of k = ceil(eps^{-1/2})), N_0 = 8, N in {8, 16, 32}. This is a scaling toward the paper's regime eps -> 0 (q -> 0 with q = eps^{1/h}), NOT the pinned q: at the pinned h the paper's own k = ceil(q^{-h/2}) equals 2 for every q > 2^{-2/h}. Lambda := lambda_0 L_s (the paper's L_s ~ S_*) is a second scaling parameter, Lambda in {500, 1000, 2000}.
claimed.hierarchy_claim_P3: Proposition 9.1 (pp. 101-102) and its table: with the principal operator L_m(a,pi) = Q^{1+h} N_abs a + K a + eps k^2 m^2 |n_Phi|^2 a + ikm n_Phi pi (9.1), the remainder (9.2) consists of seven groups whose gains above the amplitude's exponent alpha are: slow transport (-eps d_T + b D_r + G D_z)a: 1 - kappa_s; phase transport defect ikm E_ik a: 1/2; base derivatives and connections a_r(d_R b)e_r + a_z D_z(b,V,G) + (b/R)a_theta e_theta: 1; pressure-amplitude gradient (D_r pi, 0, D_z pi): 1/2 - kappa_s; viscous amplitude derivatives -eps(D_r^2 + R^{-1}D_r + D_z^2)a - eps R^{-2}(a_r,a_theta,0): 1 - 2 kappa_s; mixed derivatives and phase divergence 2ikm eps(n_r D_r + n_z D_z)a + ikm eps(D_r n_r + n_r/R + D_z n_z)a: 1/2 - kappa_s; viscous angular connection 2ikm eps(n_theta/R)(-a_theta, a_r, 0): 1/2; common lower bound alpha + 1/2 - 3 kappa_s, 'polynomial factors of S_*' permitted. Each gain g means the term is smaller than the leading terms by eps^g = q^{h g} up to S_* powers. The q^{2h} statements: (5.42) p. 60, base corrections u_B - u^{(0)} = O(q^{2h}); p. 26, 'the remaining radial terms, and axial viscosity relative to radial viscosity in the tangential equations, carry an additional factor at least q^{2h}'. PRE-RUN NOTE: at h = 1e-7 the claimed exponents h g are <= 1e-7 and at h = 1e-3 they are <= 1e-3, both far inside the pre-registered +-0.05 window, so the exponent clause of P3 cannot discriminate at either pinned h; the magnitude clause ('smaller than the leading term') is the operative one and is expected, before running, to FAIL at the pinned F_0 ~ 1e-240 by a factor of order 1/(F_0 lambda_0) ~ 1e243 (chart slow rates are O(1), pulse rates are O(F_0 sqrt(h))). The paper's own admissibility condition S_*^2 (eps + eps^2 + k^{-1}) <= 1 (p. 77) with S_* = l^2, eps = 2^{-hl}, k = ceil(eps^{-1/2}) is solved for the smallest band index l_min and reported as log10 q_* = -l_min log10 2.

instantiated_vs_scaled: Instantiated at the pinned interface (lambda = 0.1 tail, both h, Q = q): the tail frame (g_0 = (-aF_0, 0), lambda_0 = sqrt(2(a-2))F_0, c_0 = -lambda_0/(2F_0)), the exact homogeneous pulse of Lemma 7.4 on the moving plane, its (7.21) structure, the covariance columns (7.27)-(7.28), the positive inversion (7.24) for the pinned T_0 at every slow point and eta, and the identity (7.26) re-assembled from explicit products (theta-entry to float precision; z-entry only through the exact sigma-split, since T_z/T_theta ~ 1e-137). Everything that depends on the SIZE of the pulse relative to the base is a scaling: at the pinned tail F_0 = E/R is 10^-240..10^-239 in chart units, so (i) the viscous balance eps k^2 B_s^2 ~ lambda_0 puts the carrier wavelength 2pi/(kB_s) at 10^18.5..10^18.6 times the annulus radius R ~ 10^103.7 at every eps <= 1, i.e. the 'pulse' is not a wave on the annulus; (ii) the angular wavenumber the paper must round to a nonzero integer, k p~, is ~1e-25 at the pinned point, so the rounding to kp = 1 changes the phase normal by 10^25 and (7.9) fails; (iii) the wave amplitude needed to carry T_0 is 10^33..10^119 times the base velocity E (10^137..10^223 times F_0), so the paper's hierarchy (waves O(sqrt(eps)) below an O(1) base) is inverted; (iv) the pulse's own rates are O(F_0 sqrt(h)) while the chart's slow rates are O(1), so every (9.2) remainder exceeds the principal operator by 10^10..10^269. The scalings toward the paper's regime that were measured: the Lambda = lambda_0 L_s -> infinity limit ((7.21), (7.28): exponents -1.00, -1.00 against the paper's bounds -1 and -1/2), the eps -> 0 limit under eps k^2 = 4 with N = k in {8,16,32} (exact-curl covariance defect exponent -6.00 against the bound -1+2kappa_s; the pointwise curl remainder exponent -1.00 against the bound -1+2kappa_s), and the 'paper regime' variant F_0 := 1, R := 1 in which the exact-curl defect is 1.4e-18 (h = 1e-7) and the (9.2) groups still exceed the leading terms by up to 1e9 at eps ~ 1 because of Lambda/lambda_0 and mu^2/(r_0^2 lambda_0), with crossover log10 q given per group. The paper's own admissibility S_*^2(eps + eps^2 + 1/k) <= 1 (p. 77) needs l >= 2.50e+09, i.e. log10 q <= -7.52e+08 at h = 1e-7 (l >= 1.36e+05, log10 q <= -4.11e+04 at h = 1e-3); the pinned profile adds log10 q <= -2.38e+09 (h = 1e-7) for the waves to fall below the base velocity and for the carrier wavelength to fit inside R. No computable q is in the paper's regime for this interface.
could_not_determine: I could not determine the base radial velocity V_0 on the tail, because it is fixed by the axial-flux moment M = int U dx of the axis construction (4.7), which this unit does not build (leg 432 H8 records the same gap); the (9.2) groups containing b = eps V_0/(L sqrt(2X)) were bounded with |V_0| <= 1 and are upper bounds.

I could not determine the transverse rectangle half-width r_0 of Lemma 6.1, because the paper fixes it only as 'small enough' with no value; r_0 = 0.1 was used; the wave amplitude scales as 1/r_0 and the transverse-derivative terms as 1/r_0 and 1/r_0^2, so the P3 magnitudes carry this choice (their exponents in eps do not).

I could not determine a convergence order in N for the prescribed-amplitude covariance, because the paper states (7.26) as an identity; the exponent clause of P1/P2 was therefore evaluated against the class bound of Lemma 7.7/Corollary 7.8 for the exactly divergence-free field, with the one-sided reading fixed in `claimed` before any number. Under the literal two-sided +-0.3 window around -1 the measured -6.00 fails; under the pre-registered one-sided reading it passes. Both are reported; the gate answers do not rest on this clause.

I could not resolve the z-entry of the Reynolds stress from explicit float64 products at the pinned target, because T_z/T_theta is 1e-137 and the paper realises it as the sigma-antisymmetric difference of two O(T_theta/sqrt(h)) products; it is reproduced only through the exact sigma-split algebra (error ~1e-16), which is an algebraic identity, not an independent check.

I could not test the principal cancellation (9.1) independently, because the stored pulse is the RK4 solution of that operator; the exactness of the two-dimensional reduction (constraint preservation, U^l U' = 0) was derived by hand from (7.6)-(7.8) and encoded, not checked against a three-dimensional integration within the budget.

The eta-derivative entering D_z was taken analytically (d/deta log T_theta = 4 h eta/L at eta = 0.5) rather than by finite differences, because the finite difference of the eta = +-0.5 solves vanishes by the evenness of L; the level-2 pulses and amplitudes are those of eta = 0.

S_* was identified with Lambda in the level-2 transverse derivative and with (log2(1/q))^2 in P3 (the paper's S_* = l^2); the paper's own Lambda = lambda_0 L_s with L_s = 2r_0/c_i would be 10^{-240} at the pinned F_0 (the pulse would not evolve at all inside its window), which is why Lambda was taken as a free scaling parameter and reported as such.

gate_answer: P1 = NO, P2 = NO, P3 = NO at the pinned interface, with the exact part of Proposition 7.5 confirmed and the size hierarchy inverted. What holds: the homogeneous pulse of Lemma 7.4 built from the tail's frame has x/P in [0.55, 0.90] on its window and y/x = c_0 sqrt(1+s^2) to 2.0e-04 at Lambda = 2000 (deviation ~ Lambda^-1.00 as (7.21) says); its covariance columns have the (7.28) form with |e_sigma| = 4.1e-04 at Lambda = 2000 scaling as Lambda^-1.00 (the paper bounds S_*^-1/2); H is invertible with y_+, y_- > 0 at all 25 slow points and eta in {-0.5, 0, 0.5} for both h; and the explicit product of the prescribed-amplitude field reproduces the theta-entry of T_0 to 1.4e-16 (h = 1e-7), the same at every N, with the phase-shift control at 0.50 and the amplitude-halved control at 0.75. What fails: the paper's u_osc is the curl of a potential, and at the pinned F_0 ~ 1e-240 its covariance defect is 8.1e+221 at N = 32 (P1 clause (a): NO), its radial divergence residual 4.8e+221 (P2: NO), while in the F_0 = 1, R = 1 scaling the defect is 1.4e-18 (h = 1e-7) and 1.4e-12 (h = 1e-3) with N-exponent -6.00 (the paper's bound is -1: satisfied one-sidedly, not within +-0.3 two-sidedly). P3: at the pinned point every one of the seven (9.2) groups is LARGER than the principal operator, by 1e10 (angular connection, unrounded) to 1e269 (viscous transverse derivatives), at all three q; their measured q-exponents equal h times the paper's gains to float precision when S_* is frozen (a bookkeeping check of the explicit eps powers, vacuous against +-0.05), and the paper's hierarchy would hold only for log10 q below about -7.5e+08 (its own p. 77 condition) and -2.4e+09 (waves below the base velocity) at h = 1e-7. The stress this unit was asked to cancel is carried by the paper's algebra exactly and by its pulses not at all at any computable q. This is Tier 2, not a proof.
